approach: Add run/format.rs with `format_work_tree(dir, changes: &[DiffEntry], ctx: &CheckContext)`, Athena host code and not an agent command. When `dir/Cargo.toml` is a file and the change list holds a non-deleted `*.rs` entry, it runs `cargo fmt --all` then `cargo fmt --all --check`, both through `checks::run_check`. It returns `Skipped(reason)`, `Done`, `Unfixed{output, note}` or `Stopped(note)` (kill switch set or a run hit its deadline). `producer_loop` calls it in every pass as the last producer-stage act: right after the producer agent returned and its report was parsed (the `raw` match, producer.rs:325-335) and before the first `snapshot.change_list()` (producer.rs:339). The reading's assumption says "The format step belongs at the end of producer_loop, before the change list is taken"; this is that place. The loop's exit, `loop_replay`, the candidate, the checks and the verifier all come after it, so all see the same formatted tree. The Stopped arm closes the job with `self.failure` and returns `Flow::Stop`; a pipeline test drives it through `Athena::go`. Root cause: the producer's grant allows `cargo fmt` (policy.rs:680 denies it only to roles that cannot write), but only prose asks the producer to run it and nothing makes the tree formatted before the gate. Revision this round (answers the round-5 findings): every git demonstration now names `HEAD~1`, because the verifier's snapshot holds base then candidate as two commits and a bare `git diff`/`git status` shows nothing there; criterion 8 lists `crates/athena-context` and not the absent `skills` directory; the criterion 3 wording, format.rs module docs and the producer_loop doc comment quote the reading and say the call is the last producer-stage act of each pass.

decisions.choice: Run the format step in each producer pass, after the report is parsed and before `let changes = snapshot.change_list()?` (producer.rs:339). Take a first change list for the guard, format, and let line 339 read the list again. Document in format.rs module docs and the producer_loop doc comment, quoting the reading ('The format step belongs at the end of producer_loop, before the change list is taken'), that the call is the last producer-stage act of every pass, that 'after the producer' means after each producer invocation returns, and that the loop exit, candidate, checks and verifier all come after it.
decisions.reason: `loop_replay` (producer.rs:370) stores the tree it measured and `replay_run` reuses it only if `covers` holds, so formatting after the loop would change the candidate tree and force a rebuild of the replay pair. It would also leave the scope, gate and mirror send-back checks judging a tree that is not the candidate. The step is idempotent, so a send-back pass formats again cheaply. It still comes after the producer and before the checks and verifier (criterion 3), which a reader can verify from the doc text and the Grep.

rejected.why: The replay tree no longer matches the candidate, and the in-loop checks judge an unformatted tree. A path the formatter adds ends the job at check_and_verify with no send-back.

In producer_loop bind `let registry = self.state.registry();` before the `CheckContext` literal.

decisions.choice: Before running anything, and after each run, `format_work_tree` returns `Formatted::Stopped(note)` if `ctx.registry.stopped()` or `checks::timed_out(&run)` is true. `producer_loop` then does `closing.happened = self.failure(ctx, &format!("the format step stopped: {note}")); return Ok(Flow::Stop);`, the shape of producer.rs:292-294 and 332-333.
decisions.reason: run_check reports a kill-switch kill as a failed run with a note and exit_code None (checks.rs:577-583), not as an error. Without the arm a stopped job would go on into loop_replay, the checks and the candidate. A deadline hit is a hung tool, not a layout error, so it stops the job with the reason. The arm is proven through `Athena::go`: the fake driver checks `Registry::stopped` only before the script runs (fake.rs:92-97), so a producer script that writes the STOP file during its turn reaches the format step with the switch set.

rejected.option: Map every failed `--check` run to Unfixed
rejected.why: Hides a stop from the loop, which keeps running a job the user has stopped.

rejected.option: Return an Err from format_work_tree on stop
rejected.why: An Err from producer_loop carries no closing reason; `self.failure` records it as the other stop points do.

rejected.option: Test the Stopped arm only by calling `format_work_tree`
rejected.why: Nothing would fail if the arm forgot `return Ok(Flow::Stop)` or fell through to loop_replay and the checks.

decisions.choice: An Unfixed result changes no flow. It prints one UI line `format     cargo fmt --check still fails: <first line starting error, else first output line>; the fmt check will report it` and leaves the tree. When `work_tree_tree()` differs afterwards it prints `format     cargo fmt rewrote the work tree before the checks`, and prints `format     cargo fmt also changed <paths> beyond the producer's files` for any path from the pure helper `paths_added_by_format(before, after)`.
decisions.reason: The reading says unfixable errors stay in the tree and the normal fmt check reports them; a second reporting path could relax the gate. Naming added paths covers the base-drift case at its minimum, and the in-loop scope check, which runs after the step, still sends the producer back for a path outside its allowed paths.

rejected.option: Narrow the rewrite with `rustfmt --edition <ed> <files>` or `cargo fmt -- <files>`
rejected.why: rustfmt on a file also formats its out-of-line `mod` children; plain rustfmt does not read the package edition, so the result could differ from what `cargo fmt --all --check` accepts.

risks.risk: The tests run real cargo fmt under a cleared env. On a host with no rustup default toolchain, or a different default, cargo fmt could fail to start or use another rustfmt.
risks.mitigation: Every temp crate and the end-to-end formatting base carry the repository's pinned rust-toolchain.toml. The unit env also passes RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN when set. A host without that toolchain fails the tests rather than skipping, as it already fails its own fmt check. The stop tests start no cargo.

risks.risk: The base is not fmt-clean, so `cargo fmt --all` rewrites files the producer never touched and adds paths outside the job's allowed paths.
risks.mitigation: The step runs only when a non-deleted `.rs` entry is already in the change list. A UI line names any path it adds, and the in-loop scope check, which runs after the step, can send the producer back. The reading accepts the clean-base assumption.

risks.risk: A kill switch or hung fmt could be mistaken for a layout error and the job would go on.
risks.mitigation: The Stopped outcome ends the job through `self.failure` and `Flow::Stop`; the end-to-end stop test runs `go` and asserts Failed, the reason, no verifier call and no candidate.

risks.risk: In the stop test, closing the job after the kill switch is set might itself be refused (refuse_if_stopped at some record or landing step), hiding the Failed outcome.
risks.mitigation: `refuse_if_stopped` is at entry points (mod.rs:437, checks.rs:99/107, reading.rs, landing.rs:719), not in the failure-closing path producer.rs:292-294 uses. If the test finds otherwise, it reads the job's closed state from the records instead of the returned value; the same assertions apply.

risks.risk: `cargo fmt` may write a Cargo.lock in the end-to-end tree, which would show in the change list and break the exact-changes assertion.
risks.mitigation: `cargo fmt` reads `cargo metadata --no-deps`, which resolves nothing, and the test crate has no dependencies. If a lock file still appears, the base commits one with `commit_file`.

risks.risk: Formatting every pass costs two cargo runs per producer invocation.
risks.mitigation: A few seconds with no build; the step is idempotent and a producer rarely has more than two passes (`PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS`).

risks.risk: A pinned study mounts a checkout inside the work tree (producer.rs:147-149), and formatting would alter pinned files.
rustfmt output varies by toolchain version, so literal expected text could drift.
risks.mitigation: The pinned toolchain file fixes the version in tests; expected text uses stable constructs (`fn f( )->u32{1}`, `pub fn two( )->u32{2}`), and the long-array case is proved by the post `--check` pass.

risks.risk: A verifier git demonstration without a revision shows nothing in the base-then-candidate snapshot and so proves nothing.
risks.mitigation: Criteria 5, 6 and 8 use `git diff --stat HEAD~1` and `git diff HEAD~1 -- CHANGELOG.md`; bare `git diff` and `git status` are not evidence for the verifier. The producer's own `git status --short` self-check runs in its one-commit snapshot where it is accurate.

risks.risk: A demonstration command that is compound or rewrites files is refused to the verifier.
risks.mitigation: All demonstrations are single simple commands from the allowed list; `cargo fmt --all --check` is the only fmt form the verifier runs; `cargo fmt --all` appears only as a producer step.

risks.risk: A literal reading of criterion 3 ('after the producer loop') could mark the in-loop call unmet.
risks.mitigation: The format.rs docs, the producer_loop doc comment and the criterion 3 demonstration quote the reading's assumption (end of producer_loop, before the change list is taken) and state that the loop exit, candidate, checks and verifier all come after the call; test (b) shows the verifier-side check passes on the formatted tree.

demonstrations.method: Unit test `a_misformatted_rust_file_is_rewritten_and_cargo_fmt_check_then_passes` in run/tests.rs. `temp_crate` writes Cargo.toml, the pinned rust-toolchain.toml and a src/lib.rs with a long `pub const` array on one line and `fn f( )->u32{1}`. The CheckContext takes its env from the process (PATH, HOME, RUSTUP_HOME, CARGO_HOME, RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN when set), `Registry::new(tempdir)` and `Redactor::new(&athena_gate::builtin_config())`. Run `run_check` with `cargo fmt --all --check` and assert it fails; call `format_work_tree(dir, &[entry('M',"src/lib.rs")], &ctx)`; assert `Done`, that the text changed to rustfmt layout, and that the `--check` through `run_check` now passes.
demonstrations.observes: The file bytes change to the formatted layout, the outcome is Done, and the fmt check goes from failed to passed. The whole athena-core suite passes.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the formatter run the file stays mis-formatted, so the content, Done and post-`--check` assertions fail.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `run::format::format_work_tree` (added by plan step 1), called with a real `CheckContext` over a tempdir and real `cargo fmt` resolved by the written rust-toolchain.toml. Guards: Cargo.toml present and a non-deleted `.rs` entry. No double. `checks::run_check` exists (checks.rs:513). The test and the `temp_crate`, `entry` and context helpers are added by step 5.

demonstrations.method: Unit test `an_unfixable_fmt_error_is_reported_and_the_fmt_check_fails_with_the_same_text`. The temp crate's src/lib.rs is `pub fn broken( {`. `format_work_tree` with `entry('M',"src/lib.rs")` must return `Unfixed{output, ..}`. Take the first line of `output` that starts with `error` (the `--check` run's own capture) and assert it is non-empty. Then `run_check` with the configured spec `cargo fmt --all --check` on the same dir must give `!passed` and its `output_tail` must contain that exact line. The broken file must be byte-identical afterwards.
demonstrations.observes: A failed fmt result whose rustfmt error text appears in the failed check's output tail; the tree is unchanged and the gate is not relaxed.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the step swallowed the failure and returned Done, the Unfixed assertion fails. If it rewrote or deleted the broken file, the byte-identity assertion fails. If the check's output tail did not carry the line, the contains assertion fails.
demonstrations.seam: `format_work_tree` (step 1) plus `checks::run_check` (exists), real cargo and rustfmt in a tempdir with the pinned toolchain file. No double. Test added by step 5.

demonstrations.method: Three parts, each its own run. (a) Content: Grep crates/athena-core/src/run for `format_work_tree` and `change_list`. In producer.rs the call sits in each loop pass after the `raw` report parse (producer.rs:325-335) and before the first `snapshot.change_list()` (line 339), `loop_replay` (line 370) and the `break`; this is the reading's 'end of producer_loop, before the change list is taken', and the module docs of format.rs and the producer_loop doc comment quote that sentence and say the call is the last producer-stage act of every pass, with the loop exit, candidate, checks and verifier after it. mod.rs adds only `mod format;`; `producer_loop` returns inside `produce_and_verify` before `candidate_stage` and `check_and_verify`. (b) Behavior, formatted path: end-to-end test `a_job_whose_only_defect_is_rustfmt_layout_passes_a_cargo_fmt_check_and_the_candidate_holds_the_formatted_file` uses the real `cargo fmt --all --check` as the capability check on the verifier's snapshot; the base commits Cargo.toml, the pinned rust-toolchain.toml and a clean src/lib.rs. (c) Behavior, stop path through the pipeline: end-to-end test `a_job_stopped_during_the_producer_turn_closes_at_the_format_step_and_runs_no_check_or_verifier`. The base commits Cargo.toml and a clean src/lib.rs. A script wrapper over `counting(counts, None)` makes the producer turn edit src/lib.rs (non-deleted `.rs`, so the step is not Skipped) and also `create_dir_all` + write the STOP file at `StateDir::new(state.path().join("repo")).registry().stop_file()` (the path `athena_with` uses, tests.rs:194-196). After `go` assert: state Failed; reason contains `the format step stopped`; the `Lines` capture holds a line starting `failed     the format step stopped`; producer count 1, verifier count 0; the stored job record has no candidate and no recorded check results. Unit test `a_stopped_format_step_returns_stopped_and_leaves_the_file_untouched` covers `format_work_tree` with the STOP file under `Registry::new(tempdir)`. Part (a) uses the Grep tool.
demonstrations.observes: (b) The job reaches Landed and the real fmt check passed, so the check and verifier saw the formatted tree. (c) The job closes Failed with the format-step reason, the verifier never runs, no candidate is recorded. The unit case returns Stopped with the file byte-identical.
demonstrations.fails_without: With the `format_work_tree` call removed from producer_loop the candidate holds the mis-formatted file, the fmt check fails and the job is Rejected, not Landed. With the Stopped arm removed or not returning `Flow::Stop`, test (c) fails: the loop would go on to loop_replay, the checks and the verifier (verifier count 1, a candidate recorded, or a state other than Failed).
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `Athena::go` on the fake driver, in `produce_and_verify_order_tests`. `athena_with(repo, state, checks, plenty_of_space, script)` (tests.rs:187) wires `FakeAgentDriver::new(script).with_registry(state.registry())`; the driver checks the switch only before the script runs (fake.rs:92-97), so the STOP file written during the producer turn is first seen by the format step. `base_script()` (tests.rs:219), `counting`/`Counts` (tests.rs:2117-2184), `commit_file` (tests.rs:341), `Lines` (tests.rs:167) and `Registry::stop_file()` (procs.rs:364) exist. Steps 5-7 add the `FMT_CHECK` const, the script wrappers and the tests. Real cargo fmt runs in (b) only. The double (the script) only writes files; the formatter and the Stopped arm are production code.

demonstrations.method: The producer formats its own new code with `cargo fmt --all` (step 8) before finishing. The verifier then runs the three workspace commands separately, each a whole simple command; the formatting check is the non-writing `--check` form, so no verifier command rewrites a file. Existing fake-job tests have no Cargo.toml, so the step returns Skipped and prints nothing; the slot test at tests.rs:4185 edits README.md only, so it is Skipped too.

demonstrations.observes: All three exit 0. The new tests pass; clippy reports no warnings; `cargo fmt --all --check` reports no diff.
demonstrations.fails_without: A failing new test, a clippy warning or an unformatted new file makes the matching command exit non-zero.
demonstrations.seam: The workspace's own checks; no double. Real cargo fmt in the new tests resolves the pinned toolchain from the written rust-toolchain.toml.
